To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of radiofrequency energy in surgical or interventional procedures is associated with a very low risk for the patient with a cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED).
inactivation of ICD is recommended in all cases where surgical and/or interventional procedures are planned.

In 45 consecutive ICP patients (25 single and 10 dual chamber devices) no oversensing of electrical cauter/ radiofrequency energy occurred, no changes in the ICD programming were observed, and no damage to the device was noted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of electromagnetic radiation in medical technology.
the use of radiofrequency energy in surgical and interventional therapies in patients with implantable cardioverter‐defibrillators (ICDs).
the application of radiofrequency energy (RF) for surgical and interventional therapy in patients with an implanted cardioverter defibrillator (ICD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ICDs should not be turned off in the operating room, but that the ICD should be programmed in a way that the device is not capable of delivering a shock, and that the device is in monitoring mode only.
ICDs should not be inactivated in the presence of electrical cautery or RF energy, and that the ICD should not be located in the area of the RF application.
the application of RF in surgical or interventional procedures does not interfere with ICD function and does not pose a risk for the patient.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RF energy does not interfere with the ICDs, and the ICDs are not affected by RF energy.
the use of RF energy during surgical procedures does not pose a significant hazard to ICD patients, provided that the ICD is inactivated preoperative.

in the case of an ICD in a patient undergoing a surgical procedure or interventional therapy using electrical cautery or RF energy, the risk of interference with the ICD system is low, and therefore the ICD can be left active during these procedures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of interference between ICDs (implantable cardioverter/defibrillator) and RF energy is minimal.
the application of RF during surgical and interventional therapy does not cause undesired interactions with the ICD.
ICDs should not be turned off during surgery or intervention, but rather the device should be programmed into a monitoring mode.
